    p.field,
    p.mode,
    p.type,
    p.clean,
    p.flags,
    p.rowc,

  WHERE (
    lower(coalesce(pt.name, '')) LIKE '%star%'
    OR lower(coalesce(pt.description, '')) LIKE '%star%'
  )
),
photoobj_basic_photometry AS (
  -- choose canonical rows first; if a photoobj has no canonical row, use the star-type cohort row
  SELECT
    objid,
    run,
    rerun,
    field,
    mode,
    type,
    clean,
    flags,
    rowc,
    colc,
    cmodelmag_u,
    cmodelmag_g,
    cmodelmag_r,
    ra,
    dec,
    u, g, r, i, z,
    extinction_r
  FROM photoobj_canonical_photometry

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    objid,
    run,
    rerun,
    field,
    mode,

    clean,
    flags,
    rowc,
    colc,
    cmodelmag_u,

rows.question: Find all photometrically observable Galaxy that have spectral observations. Retrieve the object id, right ascension, and declination.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH photo_type_lookup AS (
  SELECT value, name
  FROM photo_type
),
photoobj_core AS (
  SELECT
    p.objid,
    p.ra,
    p.dec,
    p.type
  FROM photoobj p
  WHERE p.objid IS NOT NULL
    AND p.ra IS NOT NULL
    AND p.dec IS NOT NULL
),
has_spectrum AS (
  -- specobj that links to the photoobj either via bestobjid
  -- or whose specobjid appears in galspecline (meaning that spectrum is a galaxy spectrum)
  SELECT DISTINCT
    s.bestobjid AS objid
  FROM specobj s
  WHERE s.bestobjid IS NOT NULL

  UNION

  SELECT DISTINCT
    s.bestobjid AS objid
  FROM specobj s
  JOIN galspecline g ON g.specobjid = s.specobjid
  WHERE s.bestobjid IS NOT NULL

  UNION

  -- also include cases where the specobjid itself equals the photoobj.objid
  SELECT DISTINCT
    (s.specobjid)::bigint AS objid
  FROM specobj s
  JOIN galspecline g ON g.specobjid = s.specobjid
  WHERE s.specobjid IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT p.objid, p.ra, p.dec
FROM photoobj_core p
JOIN photo_type_lookup pt ON p.type = pt.value
JOIN has_spectrum h ON h.objid = p.objid
WHERE pt.name ILIKE '%galaxy%'
ORDER BY p.objid

WITH photoobj_canonical_photometry AS (
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.flags,
  p.rowc,
  p.colc,
  p.cmodelmag_u,
  p.cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.extinction_r
FROM photoobj AS p
),
photoobj_with_spec_presence AS (
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  -- boolean indicating whether there exists at least one matching spectral observation
  (s.specobjid IS NOT NULL) AS has_spec,
  -- the specobj.specobjid that matched this photoobj, if any (prefer specobj.specobjid match over bestobjid match if both exist)
  CASE
    WHEN s.specobjid IS NOT NULL THEN s.specobjid
    WHEN b.specobjid IS NOT NULL THEN b.specobjid
    ELSE NULL
  END AS matched_specobjid,
  -- the specobj.bestobjid that matched this photoobj, if any
  CASE
    WHEN s.bestobjid IS NOT NULL THEN s.bestobjid
    WHEN b.bestobjid IS NOT NULL THEN b.bestobjid
    ELSE NULL
  END AS matched_bestobjid
FROM
  photoobj AS p
  -- direct match: a specobj row whose specobjid equals this photoobj.objid
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT so.specobjid, so.bestobjid
    FROM specobj AS so
    WHERE so.specobjid = p.objid
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS s ON TRUE
  -- bestobjid match: a specobj row whose bestobjid equals this photoobj.objid, only considered if no direct match found
  LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT so2.specobjid, so2.bestobjid
    FROM specobj AS so2
    WHERE so2.bestobjid = p.objid
    LIMIT 1
  ) AS b ON s.specobjid IS NULL
),
photo_type_lookup_9 AS (
SELECT
  pt.value AS value,
  lower(pt.name) AS name,
  pt.description AS description
FROM photo_type pt
)
SELECT p.objid AS object_id,
       p.ra,
       p.dec
FROM photoobj_canonical_photometry p
JOIN photo_type_lookup_9 t ON p.type = t.value
JOIN photoobj_with_spec_presence s ON p.objid = s.objid
WHERE t.name LIKE '%galaxy%'
  AND s.has_spec = TRUE

photo_type_lookup_24 AS (
SELECT
  pt.value AS value,
  pt.name AS name,
  pt.description AS description
FROM
  photo_type pt
)
SELECT
  p.objid,
  p.run,
  p.rerun,
  p.field,
  p.mode,
  p.type,
  p.clean,
  p.flags,
  p.rowc,
  p.colc,

  p.cmodelmag_g,
  p.cmodelmag_r,
  p.cmodelmag_i,
  p.cmodelmag_z,
  p.u,
  p.g,
  p.r,
  p.i,
  p.z,
  p.ra,
  p.dec,
  p.extinction_r,
  p.mjd,
  p.loadversion
FROM photoobj_photometric_catalog p
JOIN photo_type_lookup_24 t

rows.question: Find object id, right ascension, declination of photometrically observed star whose magnitude i is brighter than 19 and fainter than 0, the difference of magnitude g and magnitude r is higher than 2.26, the difference of magnitude i and magnitude z is lower than 0.25, and either the difference of magnitude u and magnitude g is greater than 2.0 or magnitude u is fainter than 22.3
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT objid, ra, dec
FROM (
  SELECT
    p.objid,
    p.ra,
    p.dec,
    p.u,
    p.g,
    p.r,
    p.i,
    p.z,
    p.type
  FROM photoobj p
  LEFT JOIN photo_type pt ON p.type = pt.value
  WHERE
    -- keep only rows that are identified as stars by the photo_type table when available,
    -- or include rows with the raw numeric star type when the textual lookup is absent.
    (
      (pt.value IS NOT NULL AND (lower(coalesce(pt.name, '')) LIKE '%star%' OR lower(coalesce(pt.description, '')) LIKE '%star%'))
      OR pt.value IS NULL
    )
) AS cand
WHERE
  -- require all magnitudes to be present
  u IS NOT NULL
  AND g IS NOT NULL
  AND r IS NOT NULL
  AND i IS NOT NULL
  AND z IS NOT NULL
  -- magnitude and color cuts
  AND i > 0
  AND i < 19
  AND (g - r) > 2.26
  AND (i - z) < 0.25
  AND ( (u - g) > 2.0 OR u > 22.3 )

SELECT

  field,
  ra,
  dec,

  i,

rows.question: What are the photometrically observable Galaxy whose right ascension is between 140.9 and 141.1, magnitude g is brighter than 18.0 and the difference of magitude u and magnitude g is greater than 2.2. Retrieve the objecti id, right ascension and declination of these objects.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT objid, ra, dec
FROM (
  SELECT
    p.objid,
    p.ra,
    p.dec,
    p.u,
    p.g
  FROM photoobj p
  WHERE p.objid IS NOT NULL
) AS t

  AND g < 18.0
  AND (u - g) > 2.2

rows.question: Show me the object id, right ascension and declination of photometrically observed Galaxy, of which the the right ascension in a range of from 140.9 to 141.1, the magnitude g is less than 18.0 and the difference of magnitude u and g is higher than 2.2
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT p.objid,
       p.ra,
       p.dec
FROM photoobj p
JOIN photo_type pt ON p.type = pt.value
WHERE pt.name = 'GALAXY'
  AND p.ra BETWEEN 140.9 AND 141.1
  AND p.g < 18.0
  AND (p.u - p.g) > 2.2

rows.question: Find the object id, right ascension and declination of spectroscopic Galaxy, which have value of magnitude g between 17 and 18 and redshift less than 0.05.
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT
  p.objid AS object_id,
  p.ra AS right_ascension,
  p.dec AS declination
FROM photoobj p
JOIN specobj s
  ON p.objid = s.bestobjid
WHERE p.objid IS NOT NULL
  AND s.bestobjid IS NOT NULL
  AND s.class = 'GALAXY'
  AND p.g BETWEEN 17 AND 18
  AND s.z < 0.05

rows.question: Fetch me the object id, right ascension and declination of spectroscopic Galaxy with the color band magnitude g brighter than 18.0 but fainter than 17 and redshift lower than 0.05
rows.pred_sql:
SELECT p.objid, p.ra, p.dec
FROM photoobj p
JOIN specobj s ON s.bestobjid = p.objid

  AND p.g < 18.0
  AND s.z < 0.05
